page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained core configuration. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform includes advanced instruction support such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for filesystem persistence.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the single-core focus of the underlying hardware. The processor delivers strong single-threaded throughput, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2146.0. However, multi-core capacity is fundamentally constrained by the two-thread ceiling, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 2638.0 and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 1992.69. Large-block uncached memory operations register at 21.51 GB/sec for read bandwidth and 14.37 GB/sec for write bandwidth, while cached read operations reach 154.9 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications subject to per-core software licensing. By restricting execution to 2 vCPUs over 32.0 GB of RAM, it avoids unnecessary licensing fees while providing high memory headroom. The primary tradeoff lies in constrained computational parallelism and the absence of bundled local disks. Best-fit workloads include memory-heavy relational databases, in-memory key-value caches such as Redis, and lightweight ETL pipeline tasks.
